remaining_checks.question: F-13 permitted extensions and association-member distinction
remaining_checks.conclusion_or_remaining_question: Resolved. No published text imposes an extension-member rule for Observation JSON: OGC 23-002 Requirement 97 requires validity against observation.json, and both the tagged (8e03b236a049849f2ccc24b4fd9fdce5ff69bed2) and published copies of that schema define id, datastream@id (both required and readOnly), samplingFeature@id, procedure@link, phenomenonTime, resultTime, parameters, result and result@link with no additionalProperties or unevaluatedProperties keyword, so extra members (including the published Clause 16.1.5 example's foi@id) are schema-permitted; Requirement 98 and tests A.66/A.67/A.81/A.82/A.97/A.98 never examine them; no processing model (preserve, ignore, reject) is defined. The Standard's only stated posture for members a server does not accept as input is 'should be ignored' (Table 11 footnote for Command issueTime/currentStatus; Clause 9.2.2 DataStream live). Association-style @id/@link names are distinguishable by convention only (schema member names and Part 1 mapping Tables 41/43/47); no requirement, schema keyword or commonDefs.json patternProperties reserves the suffixes. RFC 7946 Section 6.1 (foreign members MAY be used; no normative processing model) governs GeoJSON documents only, and 23-002 Clause 7.2 places observations outside GeoJSON. 23-000 Requirements 9/10 (extensionIndependence/extensionRestrictions; tests A.9/A.10 are model inspections) govern the SensorML DescribedObject extension slot only. Consequences for F-13: the example defect is confirmed and sharpened (Table 7 gives the Observation only datastream, samplingFeature and procedure associations, so foi@id maps to no association at all); the inbound policy is a project choice to record, not a standards obligation; unknown-member rejection is not required and is not prescribed, and the earlier reviewer suggestion to reject or warn on unmapped @id/@link members is downgraded to an owner option that would be a labelled Glaux restriction. Documentation gap: Guide lines 406/432 (preserve permitted extensions; validated extensible payload), 497 (PATCH rejects changes outside the writable projection) and 713 (only advertised extension fields appear publicly) leave the outcome for members that are neither mapped nor advertised extensions unstated for POST/PUT/PATCH; one Section 4.6 sentence and one Section 13 row (foi@id example) would close it. Fixture set from evidence 06 Section 3.3 stands and belongs with #99's supplied sampling-feature context checks. Owning leaves 3.2.1 (#98), 3.2.2 (#99), 3.2.4-3.2.5 (#101-#102); issue bodies #98 and #99 read (no unknown-member statement). No new finding number.

material_points: Material finding of this batch: the Guide adopts the cursor, subscription and queued-decision members of IDR-040's 'cannot outlive its policy/trust bounds' invariant but not the cache member. It emits strong ETags (line 503) and Vary (line 739), names RFC 9110/9111 as an inherited dependency (line 258), and nowhere binds a validator or cache key to the authorized view, specifies any Cache-Control directive, or lists a cache channel among its disclosure tests (1019, 983). RFC 9111 Section 3.5 protects only requests carrying an Authorization header, Section 5.2.2.7's private directive is never invoked, and Section 4.1 keys Vary selection only on nominated request header fields. Two concrete consequences: a validator computed over stored state rather than the emitted authorized representation becomes an inference channel for concealed changes; and in the trusted-reverse-proxy deployments the Guide supports (364, 596), where authorization derives from a client certificate or a proxy-injected header rather than an Authorization header, an intermediary may serve one caller's authorized representation to another context.
